Maya Patel: Quick follow-up on the multi-region policy-scope experiment — wanted to capture options for guaranteeing data residency on writes while keeping active/active. TL;DR: propose adding an "x-region-policy" header + a short-lived write-intent lease so resident-region finality can be enforced without full sync pause.
Sam Gupta: sketch semantics? how does this handle "prefer" vs "enforce"?
Maya Patel: rough options:
- Option A (soft-prefer): header is advisory. Router attempts resident region first but will fallback on capacity/latency. low-tail latency.
- Option B (hard-enforce): reject or escrow at proxy if request isn't routed to resident region. strong residency guarantee but higher client-side failure surface.
- Option C (local-accept + escrow): accept locally, return provisional ack, async finalize to resident region (two-phase commit-ish but lighter).
Jordan Lee: main concerns with C: tail latency for finality, complexity for retry/idempotency, and compaction of provisional state. we need clear idempotency keys and a reconciliation sweep.
Sam Gupta: +1. also KMS boundaries: if tenant requires EU KMS, escrow cannot push plaintext to non-EU hardware. need metadata to tag encryption key scope.
Maya Patel: sample header sketch (proto):
```
x-region-policy: resident=eu-west-1;mode=hard;idempotency_key=abcd-1234
```
Router behavior pseudocode:
```
if header.mode==hard && !in_resident_region(req): return 451/residency_required
if header.mode==soft && resident_available: route_to_resident_else_fallback
if header.mode==escrow: accept_local_and_enqueue_to_resident
```
Jordan Lee: observability reqs: region_policy.enforced.count, region_policy.fallback.count, escrow.finalize_latency, and audit events with reason codes (e.g., "capacity_fallback", "consent_mismatch").
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for router parsing changes on staging (svc=region-router, tag=policy-parse-v1) :rocket:
Sam Gupta: operational questions: where does per-tenant policy live? control-plane flag per-tenant, or cluster annotation? I'd prefer control-plane so product can flip for regulated tenants.
Maya Patel: agree — control-plane per-tenant. product + infra need to own the schema. action items: 1) I'll draft an RFC with perf sims and failure modes (ETA Wed), 2) Sam to prototype header parsing + enforce/reject paths (branch region-policy-proto), 3) Jordan to draft telemetry + reconciliation sweep design.
Sam Gupta: ok i'll spin up a small prototype. will try to show basic reject vs fallback behavior with a local simulator. :ok_hand:
Jordan Lee: devex note: client SDKs should expose helper to compute header from tenant metadata; add to backlog.
Maya Patel: thanks all — tagging @Sam and @Jordan. I'll post RFC link in this thread when ready. :sparkles:
